title.en: The nervous system: neurons and coordination
Why you pull your hand from a hot pan

text.en: You touch something hot and your hand jumps away before you think. A stimulus was detected, an impulse travelled along nerves, and a response happened. The nervous system coordinates this in a fraction of a second.

A stimulus is a change in the environment detected by receptors; the body's reaction to it is the response, and working together to give a proper response is called coordination.
Coordination between cells and organs keeps the body in physiological balance, called homeostasis.
The nervous system is made of nervous tissue with three components: neurons, neuroglia and nerve fibres.
A neuron or nerve cell is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, specialised to detect, receive and transmit stimuli as electrical impulses.
A neuron has a cyton or cell body with a nucleus and Nissl's granules, dendrites that carry impulses towards the cyton, and an axon that carries impulses away.
Neuroglia are supporting glial cells that do not initiate or conduct impulses.
Neurons cannot divide, and nerve fibres are long slender processes bundled into nerves that connect receptors, the brain and effectors.

problem.en: You touch a hot vessel and pull your hand back. Trace the path from stimulus to response.

text.en: Heat is the stimulus; receptors in the skin detect it.
A sensory neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord or brain.
A motor neuron carries the command to the muscle, and the hand withdraws.

points.en: Stimulus: change detected by receptors; response: reaction.
Nervous tissue: neurons, neuroglia, nerve fibres.
Neuron = structural and functional unit; has cyton, dendrites, axon.
Neurons carry electrical impulses and cannot divide.
